sourceRef.section: NON-FACTION DOCTRINES — Consolidated Rules — Playtest Draft v6.1

title: NON-FACTION DOCTRINES

generalRules.overview: Non-Faction Doctrines represent the military strategies, tactics, and battlefield philosophies available to different armies. In 2,000-point matched play, each army selects two distinct Doctrines. Every faction may choose any two; Favored and Compatible labels are recommendations, not restrictions. Other army formats may use different numbers of Doctrines or none at all.
generalRules.structure: Each Doctrine grants one Foundation Recruitment Slot and provides five Command options. The player selects three Commands from each chosen Doctrine, gaining the Recruitment Slot listed beside each selected Command. A Doctrine Command may affect any eligible Unit unless its effect specifies otherwise. Recruitment Slots determine army composition; they do not restrict who may benefit from a Command.

commandUsage.repertoire: In standard 2,000-point matched play, the six selected Doctrine Commands and two selected Faction Commands together form an eight-card repertoire. CP and card exhaustion are the same expenditure, not cumulative costs: a printed Doctrine Command costs its listed CP and exhausts its selected card, while an eligible Unit Command instead exhausts an available selected card as the physical marker of the CP spent. A 2 CP Command requires two available cards but resolves only once. A 0 CP ability exhausts none. All exhausted cards and CP refresh at the beginning of the next Round. The full repertoire remains available, representing 8 CP for the matched-play army per Round; there is no separate two-card preparation step.
rules: Unless its wording explicitly permits a different target, a non-Reaction Faction or Doctrine Phase Command applies to the active Unit during its own activation. Reactions use their printed triggers. Explicit coordination, Reserve insertion, and multi-Unit support effects are exceptions; a player may not use a single-target buff on an arbitrary unactivated ally.

One personal Unit, Faction, or Doctrine Command per friendly Unit activation; one eligible opposing Reaction. An Attack, Charge, or Save sequence benefits from at most one friendly Command effect, including one prepared during a prior Phase. Passive bonuses are unaffected.
Each selected Command costs 1 CP unless otherwise stated. A selected card cannot be used again until refreshed.

Phase Commands are activated while the controlling side has activation priority during the indicated Movement, Assault, or Combat Phase. Personal Unit Commands instead occur during that Unit's own activation.
Reactions are used at their specified triggers regardless of activation priority. End Step Commands use their explicitly printed timing.
Commands do not grant additional Unit activations or Attacks unless explicitly stated.

Bonuses to Attacks add dice to one Attack made by the entire Unit, not to each Model, unless explicitly written per Model. Unit-wide Accurate, Critical, Tough, Cover, and Brace ranks do not multiply by Model count; compatible additional ranks are additive.
An effect applying to one Attack expires when that Attack is fully resolved.
Effects lasting a Phase expire at the end of that Phase.
Effects lasting a Round expire during that Round's End Step.
An effect referring to a Unit's next Attack or activation remains available until that event occurs or its stated duration expires.
Multiple applications of the same Command do not stack on one Unit.

An expressly refreshed Movement activation makes a Unit with a spent Movement activation eligible for a later activation in normal alternating order; it does not create an immediate Move, lift Withdrawn, reset Heavy eligibility, override Disengage, reopen a Finished side, or restore an Assault/Combat activation. Advance Orders may refresh a given Unit once per Round.
commandUsage.rpgCampaignException: A campaign party may have 2 abstract CP per player and no physical cards at all. The eight-card Doctrine repertoire is a matched-play army-construction feature, not a prerequisite for personal Commands. The controlling GM uses the encounter-specific allocation (normally max(2, 2 × number of PCs − 1)).

movementAndPositioning.chargeX: Add X inches to the final Charge distance after rolling. Standard Units roll 2D6, add the results, and compare the total (plus X) to the distance needed to Engage; the Unit's Move is not added. The highest die still sets base Charge Impact. Charge X does not modify the dice themselves or the Charge's Impact. Multiple Charge X effects do not stack; use the highest value. The normal 12" maximum distance for declaring a Charge still applies. PCs use a Body + Athletics Charge Check (Rogues may use Agility + Athletics), the two highest dice for distance, and allocate each Athletics Success to +1 inch distance or +1 Impact.
movementAndPositioning.blinkX: An unengaged Unit may reposition up to X inches without traversing intervening terrain, subject to normal elevation restrictions. For multi-model Units, move a lead Model up to X inches from its original position, then place each remaining Model no more than X inches from its own original position while maintaining Coherency. Every Model must end legally, and no Model may finish Engaged. Blink is not a Charge.
movementAndPositioning.holdingPosition: Where an ability requires a Unit to have remained in position, its wording specifies the applicable period. A Unit that voluntarily Moved, Disengaged, Charged, or Blinked during that period does not qualify. Enemy-forced movement does not count unless specifically stated.
movementAndPositioning.noStationaryKeyword: No separate Stationary keyword is used.

defensiveEffects.accurateX: Reroll up to X natural 1s during a Hit roll.
defensiveEffects.toughX: Reroll up to X natural 1s during an Armor Save roll.
defensiveEffects.braceX: Subtract X from the total automatic Charge Impact Hits suffered by the defender, to a minimum of zero. Brace does not grant retaliatory Attack dice.
defensiveEffects.hitCancellation: When an ability discards a successful non-6 Hit die, resolve it after Hit rerolls but before saves. Natural 6s, automatic Hits, and Charge Impact cannot be discarded this way.
defensiveEffects.attackReduction: When an ability removes an Attack die, remove it before the Hit roll. An Attack cannot be reduced below one die unless an ability explicitly allows it.

surgesAndBlunders.generalRule: A normal Skill Check or Charge roll generates at most one Surge (two or more natural 6s) and one Blunder (two or more natural 1s), determined after rerolls, unless specified otherwise. An Attack roll generates one Surge per complete pair of natural 6s and one Blunder per complete pair of natural 1s. An effect phrased "when this Attack Surges" normally triggers once per Attack; "for each Surge" explicitly scales.
surgesAndBlunders.recklessRoll: A roll designated Reckless cannot benefit from any rerolls. Its Surges and Blunders resolve normally, and any listed Gambit Blunder consequence applies in addition to other applicable effects.

knownIssues: At least one faction/generic Doctrine name collision exists: Free Realms' Faction Rule is named 'Combined Arms', identical to Doctrine 1 'Combined Arms', but the two have unrelated effects (see rules_data_json/factions/00_general_roster_rules.json knownIssues). Likely intentional thematic echo, not a merge.
